title: Chart preimages of a section-preserving projective pair are generating loci
statement: Let $X,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a coordinate type, $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $s_i\in\Gamma(X,M)$, and $\varphi:X\to\mathbf P(I;S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Suppose an isomorphism $\varepsilon:\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)\to M$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-pc-module-pullback] sends every pulled-back coordinate $T_i$ to $s_i$. Then for every $i\in I$ the open $\varphi^{-1}D_+(T_i)$ equals the generating locus of $s_i$ [def-sc-section-generating-locus]. No invertibility assumption on M is required separately.

source.place: Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), chart construction and uniqueness, specialized to degree-one polynomial coordinates

proof.text: The chart frame lemma proves that each point in the chart preimage lies in the generating locus. Conversely, at a point where s_i generates choose any standard chart j containing its image. The chart relation s_i=φ*(T_i/T_j)s_j and the free frame s_j imply that φ*(T_i/T_j) is a unit there. Thus the point lies in the preimage of the basic open of T_i/T_j, which is contained in D_+(T_i). This is the existing source proof generatingLocus_eq_preimage_standardOpen (LinearCombination.lean:59-67), using mem_basicOpen_of_generatesAt and basicOpen_coordRatio_le.
